title: Prefill-aware request packer with padding savings
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: High variance in sequence lengths across served requests leads to large padding overhead at prefill time. Current prefill + decode scheduling packs requests by arrival time which produces micro-batches with wide seqlen spread. This inflates memory usage and per-token cost because kernels run on padded token lengths. Additionally, prefill and decode are scheduled independently, losing opportunities to reuse KV cache placement and optimize kernel selection for the common prefix distribution.

Goal: Implement a prefill-aware request packing/coalescing layer ("Prefill Packer") that groups and shapes micro-batches using predicted decode trajectories to minimize padding while preserving latency SLOs and kernel-friendly batch shapes. The feature should operate online with bounded overhead and fall back to the legacy coalescer when signals are missing.

Design overview:
- Request annotations: Extend incoming request metadata with lightweight predictions (predicted decode length or decode distribution percentile). Predictions come from: client hints, fast local estimator (based on prompt tokens, instruction tag, and recent user session stats), or a simple ML model served locally.
- Two-stage packing: 1) Prefill bucketing: at prefill time, bucket requests by predicted total sequence length percentiles (e.g., 50/75/90). 2) Micro-batch shaping within bucket: apply pad-to-percentile and small greedy coalescing to form micro-batches with tight seqlen variance (target CV < 0.12).
- Prefill-decode affinity: Track prefill micro-batch membership and attempt to schedule decode-time requests back onto the same GPU where prefills ran when KV reuse and low-latency are available (affinity window). If affinity misses occur, fall back to best-effort kernel selection for decode.
- Kernel hints: Emit kernel-selection hints from the packer (e.g., small-prefix-optimized attention kernel, fp16-quantized path) based on bucket characteristics and sequence length distribution so the runtime can choose the best kernel quickly without extra profiling.
- Fused attention optimizations: Where a bucket's seqlen is below an attention-fusion threshold, route through fused/packed attention kernels that reduce per-token overhead. For long-tail buckets, select streaming-friendly attention kernels.
- Online histogram & throttling: Maintain a lightweight online histogram of recent seqlens to dynamically recompute percentile pad targets every minute. If buckets drift (e.g., sudden spike of long requests), the packer enlarges pad targets to avoid excessive scheduling latency and triggers a throttling signal to route heavy requests to dedicated capacity.

Trade-offs and safety:
- Prediction vs. cold-start: Relying on predicted decode lengths yields large wins but risks mispredictions. We mitigate by: using conservative percentiles for cold or low-confidence cases; enabling an immediate fallback to legacy coalescer; and tracking per-client confidence to improve estimator.
- Latency vs. cost: Aggressive bucketing reduces padding but may increase wait time to form tight micro-batches. We enforce an absolute latency cap (e.g., max_hold_ms=12ms) and measure tail latency. Buckets hitting the cap will flush early.
- Kernel complexity: Adding kernel hints increases coupling between packer and runtime. We keep hints advisory and ensure runtime still executes safe default kernels if hint verification fails.

Metrics & targets: (measured on internal conversational workload sample set)
- Padding token reduction target: >=25% relative to baseline; stretch goal 40%.
- Cost-per-generated-token improvement: 12-20% reduction for mixed seqlen workload.
- p50/p95/p99 latency: maintain within +10% of baseline (no regressions), p99 tail should not exceed SLA by more than 5% during rollout canary.
- Overhead: packer CPU <2% of worker CPU, memory for histograms <1% of process RSS.

Rollout plan:
1) Spike & prototype (done): local simulator + unit tests.
2) Canary (10% traffic, specific non-critical orgs): feature flag gated; runtime reports padding_savings metric and affinity hit rate.
3) Gradual ramp (10 -> 50 -> 100) with automated rollback on padding_savings <10% or p99 latency degradation >10%.
4) GA: move to on by default with dashboard tiles exposing per-customer pad reduction and kernel-hint effectiveness.

Docs & artifacts: design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Prefill-Aware+Request+Packer ; prototype repo spike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482 ; perf dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/prefill/packer-perf ; benchmark harness: scripts/bench/prefill_packer_bench.py in runtime repo.
